title: Part 3 Practice: Rainfall Regions and Agro-ecological Zones

questions.text: The LARGEST rainfall region in Ethiopia is:
questions.explanation: The SUMMER rainfall region (Kiremt-dominant) is the LARGEST, covering central, western, and northern highlands. It receives rain from June-August via the southwest monsoon.

questions.text: The ALL YEAR-ROUND rainfall region is located in:
questions.explanation: The ALL YEAR-ROUND rainfall region is in the SOUTHWESTERN HIGHLANDS (Jimma, Illubabor, Bench Maji). It receives rain throughout the year with no distinct dry season — perfect for coffee and dense forests.

questions.text: The WINTER rainfall region is found in:
questions.explanation: The WINTER rainfall region is the SMALLEST, found in NORTHERN AFAR near the Red Sea. It receives limited rain (<500mm) during December-February due to Red Sea influence.

questions.text: The AUTUMN and SPRING rainfall region is important for:
questions.explanation: The AUTUMN/SPRING rainfall region (southern/southeastern Ethiopia) is important for PASTORALISTS — the rains support grass regrowth for livestock. This region includes Borena and Somali areas.

questions.text: Which agro-ecological zone is BEST for coffee production?
questions.explanation: WEYNA DEGA (1,500-2,300m, 15-20°C) is IDEAL for coffee production. This zone has moderate temperatures, adequate rainfall, and fertile soils. Sidama and Jimma coffee regions are in this zone.

questions.text: The BERHA zone is characterized by:
questions.explanation: BERHA (below 500m) is the HOTTEST and DRIEST zone with temperatures above 30°C and rainfall below 500mm. Found in Afar and Somali lowlands. Used primarily for pastoralism.

questions.text: The WURCH zone is found at:
questions.explanation: WURCH (alpine zone) is found above 3,200m — in Simien and Bale Mountains. Temperatures below 10°C, frost possible, limited crops (barley only), mainly used for pasture.

questions.text: Examine the zones diagram. Which is the KOLLA zone?
questions.diagram: <svg width='350' height='200' viewBox='0 0 350 200'><rect width='350' height='200' fill='#111827' rx='8'/><rect x='40' y='15' width='270' height='30' fill='#f43f5e'/><text x='175' y='35' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='9'>Zone 1: Above 3200m</text><rect x='40' y='50' width='270' height='30' fill='#facc15'/><text x='175' y='70' text-anchor='middle' fill='#0B0F19' font-size='9'>Zone 2: 2300-3200m</text><rect x='40' y='85' width='270' height='30' fill='#14b8a6'/><text x='175' y='105' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='9'>Zone 3: 1500-2300m</text><rect x='40' y='120' width='270' height='30' fill='#38bdf8'/><text x='175' y='140' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='9'>Zone 4: 500-1500m</text><rect x='40' y='155' width='270' height='30' fill='#f59e0b'/><text x='175' y='175' text-anchor='middle' fill='#0B0F19' font-size='9'>Zone 5: Below 500m</text></svg>
questions.explanation: Zone 4 (blue, 500-1,500m) is KOLLA — warm lowland zone. Zone 1 = Wurch, Zone 2 = Dega, Zone 3 = Weyna Dega, Zone 5 = Berha.

questions.text: Which crops grow BEST in the KOLLA zone?
questions.explanation: KOLLA (500-1,500m, 20-30°C) is suited for SORGHUM and COTTON — crops that tolerate warm temperatures. Barley/wheat are DEGA crops. Coffee/teff are WEYNA DEGA crops.

questions.text: The DENSE forests of southwestern Ethiopia are supported by:
questions.explanation: The DENSE forests of southwestern Ethiopia (Jimma, Illubabor) are supported by ALL YEAR-ROUND rainfall (above 2,000mm). This constant moisture supports coffee forests, bamboo, and rich biodiversity.
